name: Satan and the Fall of the Angels
path: Angelology: The Doctrine of Spiritual Beings

objectives.text: Identify from the story in Genesis 3 that the serpent tempted Adam and Eve to disobey God
Recall that God made all the angels good and that some of them chose to turn against Him
Name Satan as the leader of the fallen angels and the enemy of God and His people
Recall Jesus' teaching that Satan is a liar and the father of lies
Retell how the serpent twisted God's words in the garden by comparing God's command with the serpent's question
Describe how the angels who sinned left their proper place and are kept for God's judgment
Explain the Reformed teaching that the devil was created good and fell through pride
Explain from the opening chapters of Job that Satan can act only within the limits God sets
Compare Satan's limited power and knowledge as a creature with God's unlimited power and knowledge
Identify the names and titles Scripture gives to Satan and explain what each reveals about his character
Analyze Satan's works as accuser, tempter, and deceiver in key passages of Scripture
Explain how Satan's temptation led humanity into sin while Adam and Eve remained responsible for their own disobedience
Interpret Genesis 3:15 as God's first promise of a Redeemer who would crush the serpent
Explain the Reformed teaching that God's providence extends to the fall of the angels without making God the author of sin
Explain why Scripture offers no redemption to fallen angels in contrast to its offer of redemption to fallen humanity
Evaluate readings of Isaiah 14 and Ezekiel 28 as descriptions of Satan's fall in light of their original setting as oracles against the kings of Babylon and Tyre
Construct a biblical account of the origin, fall, and final end of Satan from carefully chosen texts
Evaluate popular depictions of the devil as a cartoon villain, the ruler of hell, or God's equal opposite against the teaching of Scripture
Defend the reality of a personal and malevolent devil against claims that he is only a symbol of evil
Synthesize the biblical teaching that Satan's rebellion is real and serious yet wholly under God's rule and destined for defeat

changes: Corrected every Jude citation to the valid chapter and verse form Jude 1:6. Kept and reworded the real competencies on the angelic rebellion, Satan as enemy and liar, the temptation in Eden, creation good and fall by pride, Satan's limits, his works, Genesis 3:15, providence, a constructed account, popular myths, skepticism, and a final synthesis. Dropped the watchfulness objective because practical resistance belongs to Demons and Spiritual Warfare. Added objectives on the serpent's twisting of God's word, the titles of Satan, human responsibility in the Fall, the absence of redemption for fallen angels, and the interpretation of Isaiah 14 and Ezekiel 28 in their original setting. Added Belgic Confession Article 12, WCF 5.4, WCF 6.1, WLC Q21, and WSC Q20 where they state the doctrine taught.
